title: introduce-deferential-load-shed-and-microfailover-stabilizer
author: Aisha Rahman
description:
Motivation: During a cross-region CPU pressure incident we observed large variance in tenant impact: high-priority tenants degraded gracefully while low-priority tenants experienced abrupt drops. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: 1) a deferential load-shedder that computes per-tenant, per-route soft-shed scores using SLO budgets, recent error/latency signals, and region capacity pressure; and 2) a microfailover stabilizer that performs fast, connection-preserving microfailovers to standby pools for a narrow subset of failing routes, reducing whole-region fail blasts. Key goals: reduce noisy eviction cascades, maintain latency SLOs for high-priority tenants, and provide observability and runtime knobs for ops to tune behavior. Scope: runtime serving (shedder, microfailover), control-plane flags (per-tenant policy), default config, docs and ops runbook. The description below lists changes, design notes, tests and rollout plan.

Design summary: deferential_shedder computes a sliding-window budget deficit and an urgency multiplier derived from recent p95/p99 latency spikes and error rates. The final soft-shed score is normalized against a tenant weight and route importance; scores map to probabilistic early-deny or token-trim factors. The microfailover_stabilizer watches in-flight connection health and, when a protected route exhibits connection-level failure patterns, triggers an atomic microfailover to a warm standby maintaining KV-cache hints where possible. Microfailovers are rate-limited and histogramed to avoid mass rebalancing.

Runtime knobs and flags added: runtime.shedder.deferential_enabled (bool), runtime.shedder.window_secs (int), runtime.shedder.base_prob_table (yaml), runtime.failover.micro_enabled (bool), runtime.failover.max_per_minute (int), runtime.failover.preserve_kv_hint (bool). Defaults are conservative: deferential_enabled=true, micro_enabled=false (opt-in during canary).

Backward compatibility and safety: configuration defaults preserve current behavior unless micro_enabled=true. Deferential shedder is additive to existing batch/prefix caches and will only probabilistically reduce admission; we add a global override that sets all tenants to pass-through for emergency. We included a killswitch endpoint and a circuit metric that ops can use to fully disable the mechanism in emergencies.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics: shedder.score_distribution (hist), shedder.actions{allow,probabilistic_deny,trim}, microfailover.attempts, microfailover.successes, microfailover.kv_preserve_rate. Traces tagged with shed_score and microfailover_id for downstream correlation. Added a Redwood Console dashboard panel and alert playbook entries in docs/ops/deferential_shed.md.

Testing: unit tests for score computation, randomized property tests for probabilistic deny bounds, integration harness that runs a synthetic tenant-mix under CPU pressure and validates percentile preservation for high-priority tenants. CI includes a smoke-canary step that simulates a limited microfailover target.

Migration and rollout: staged rollout plan: enable deferential_shedder in canary region (10% traffic) with micro_enabled=false; observe metrics for one week, then enable microfailover in a narrow subset of routes (non-critical) and validate. Full enable only after SRE sign-off.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc attached (ENG-3421)
- [x] unit and integration tests
- [x] metrics and dashboard panels
- [x] ops runbook and killswitch
- [x] staged rollout plan

Risks and mitigations: probabilistic shedding could bias certain tenant cohorts; mitigated by tenant-weight normalization and fairness smoothing. Microfailover could lose KV-coherence; mitigated by soft-preserve hints and a conservative default off.

Related: builds on previous regional-shed and circuit work (SRE-77) but takes a different approach by combining soft probabilistic denial with microfailover rather than wholesale tenant eviction.

release_notes: Adds a deferential probabilistic load-shedder (opt-in) and a microfailover stabilizer (opt-in) to reduce noisy eviction cascades and preserve high-priority tenant SLOs during regional pressure. Disabled-by-default microfailover; conservative defaults and ops controls included.
notes_for_ops: Docs at docs/ops/deferential_shed.md. Default conservative rollout. Killswitch available at /admin/runtime/kill-switch?feature=deferential_shed. Monitor shedder.actions and microfailover.attempts during canary.
